title: Next ID
statement: Works out the next free ID for a record of a kind under a parent: the kind's ID pattern with the parent's, domain's or product's ID put in, numbered one past the highest number any record of that pattern has, so an ID once used is never given again.

title: Check order
statement: Orders the check rows for a run and for the reference: Lathe's checks by position, then each product's by position, so a product check never changes which of Lathe's problems are found.

title: Space look and place
statement: A product's icon MUST be its `icon` field when that is one emoji or up to two characters, and otherwise its ID as a monogram. Its color MUST be its `color` field when that is a hex color or a color name, and otherwise one derived from its ID, the same on every visit. Spaces MUST be in the products' ID order everywhere they are listed, and the nth space MUST be the one Alt+n opens.

title: Current space
statement: The current space MUST be the product of the page on screen when it belongs to one (its product, domain, record or group page, or its Checks page); on a page outside every space (the products, the format, Settings) it MUST stay the space last chosen, or the first product.

title: Folder placement
statement: Places a product's records in the nav's tree, read by the nav, the domain page, the group pages and the graph alike (DR19). A product holds Shared (its patterns and standards, and each record with no owner, a value object, view, integration or UI component, that two or more domains use, or none, with what sits under it), then its domains, then its open questions. A record with no owner that one domain uses sits in that domain, in its kind's stage and folder, as the store places it (`LA-PLT-UC01-R05`). A domain holds its five stages in the schema's order, `schema.stages`, each named by its own label, then its open questions. A record sits in its kind's stage: at the top of the stage when its parent is its domain or of another stage, or it has none (a flow under its use case, a handler under its command, a test under its obligation, a view), and under its parent when the parent is of the same stage, reached through it (DR21). A kind in no stage gets a folder of its own after the stages. Within a stage, kinds come in the schema's order (Test plan's ten test kinds in the plan's order), and records with a `position` (capabilities, flow steps) come by it, then by ID, with the records outside any capability last. An empty stage or kind group is never shown.

title: Graph tree
statement: The graph's tree is the nav's tree, from DS03: the product, its Shared, then its domains, each holding its five stages, their kind groups and the records in them. A kind group is derived from its parent and the kind of its children, never a record: it has no ID of its own, only its address, and no record links to it.

title: Tree map layout
statement: Each product MUST have a graph of its own: its tree laid out once per load of the specs, as one icicle with the product as its single root, then its Shared folder (its own stages), its domains, their stages, folders and records and their children, as the nav's tree has them (`LA-EXP-DS04`). No node, link, hint or minimap box of another product MAY be in it; a record no product reaches is the root of a map of its own. A node's size MUST come from the tree alone, top-down from the product's fixed box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), never from what is in focus: the product's box is as wide as it is tall; a parent's children split its height equally, a gap apart of a tenth of each one's part, their stack filling it from its top edge to its bottom edge, in the tree's order; and a parent's children form a column of their own, all as wide as each other: 0.4 times their parent's width, but never wider than 6 times their own height, so the more children share a parent, the narrower their column, and no box is flatter than 6 to 1. Each column starts a gap of 0.15 times its width after its parent. Each label is centered in its box. Each parent line MUST be drawn level, at the child's middle, from the parent's outline to the child's. Nothing in the map is ever laid out again or resized while the person walks it; filters hide nodes without moving the rest. A trace is a chain, not a tree, and keeps a small picture of its own, in columns of 190 by 56 boxes at text scale 1, each as tall as its wrapped label if taller. In the graph, every record or group with the same parent MUST sit in the same column, whatever its kind, so no sibling is further left or further right than another. A column is a depth in the parent/child tree around the focus; within a column, siblings MUST stay together, ordered by their parent's place, then by kind, then by ID. The same specs MUST always give the same map, and the same focus, depth, filters and mode the same framed picture, so walking the graph is predictable: records in one column keep their order, and their places, whatever is in focus.

title: Label fitting
statement:
One rule MUST size every layout of the graph (Tree, Nested and Voronoi), top-down from one fixed product box: siblings are the same size, with the same text. The product's box MUST have a fixed size, the same for every product (300,000 map units), and each parent MUST split its room equally among its children, in the tree's order. Record counts and titles MUST size no box: a busy sibling packs its children smaller, and a quiet one has blank space. How each layout splits its room is `LA-EXP-DS05` (Tree), `LA-EXP-DS07` (Nested) and `LA-EXP-DS08` (Voronoi).

A node's label is part of the map. A box's text scale MUST be at most a fixed share of its box's size, the same share at every depth: in the Tree its width over 250 map units (siblings share one width, as `LA-EXP-DS05` sets it from their height); in Nested its side, and in Voronoi the square root of its area, over 400 map units. Siblings MUST share one text scale: the largest, at most that share, at which every sibling's whole label fits its room, its kind and ID line and its title wrapped on whole words, with its padding, its marks, its shape's room and its border. So a framed box's header reads at about the same size on screen (in the Tree within a fifth of each other) whichever box is framed, and very small boxes have very small text, read by zooming in. Its title, its kind and ID line, its padding and its problem badge MUST grow by that scale, in map units, whatever the person's text size; its border, outline and parent line's stroke grow with it too (never below half in the Nested and Voronoi views), so a box's edge stays in proportion to its label; a trace's boxes are at text scale 1. The text MUST never change size relative to its box: not when the focus changes, not when the camera zooms or settles; only the camera changes how big it looks. Every drawn box shows its label at that size, however small it is on screen (`LA-EXP-DS10`, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`).

A title MUST wrap on whole words, after a space, never cut off or ended with an ellipsis; only a word too wide for a line on its own MAY break, after a hyphen (or a slash in a file's path) first, and the text scale never lets that happen in a map. The kind and ID line MAY wrap too. Lines MUST be broken when the map is built, measured by the canvas's own text metrics in the label's faces once they have loaded (the theme's body and mono faces), and the canvas MUST draw exactly those lines in those faces, so the map is laid out once per spec load and its faces, and is the same every time for a given face. Each line's height MUST be in proportion to its text, so no glyph is clipped. Map units MUST be kept in doubles, never rounded, so the deepest boxes keep their places however small they are against the product's box.

title: Nested map layout
statement:
In the Nested view the graph MUST lay out the same tree as the Tree view (`LA-EXP-DS04`), its product's alone with the product as its single root and nothing of another product, once per load of the specs, as nested squares, top-down from the product's fixed square by `LA-EXP-DS06`'s rule: siblings are the same size, with the same text. A parent's room under its header band, inside its padding, MUST hold its children as a grid of equal squares in the tree's order, row by row, a gap apart, with the column count that makes the squares largest; room the grid leaves is blank. The padding and the gaps are shares of the box's side (8 and 6 at its side's text scale), so the layout is the same at any size. Siblings share one text scale, their side over 400 map units or the largest below it at which every sibling's whole label fits: a leaf's centered in its square, a parent's in a header band at most a quarter of its square. Siblings share one header band too, as tall as the tallest of their labels at that scale. Record counts size nothing.

A box with children MUST show its label in its header band at its top and hold its children below it, so no two siblings overlap and no child leaves its parent. A label's kind and ID line and its title each wrap on whole words, never inside one, and nothing is clipped: a leaf's label is centered in it, a parent's sits at the top left of its header band. Every drawn box shows its label (`LA-EXP-DS10`). A domain is a square there, with a small hexagon mark in its header (`LA-V93-R05` holds in the Tree view). The focus never changes the map, and filters hide boxes without moving the rest. No parent lines are drawn: holding is the parent link.

title: Voronoi map layout
statement:
In the Voronoi view the graph MUST lay out the same tree as the Tree view (`LA-EXP-DS04`), its product's alone with the product as its single root, once per load of the specs, as a Voronoi treemap, top-down from the product's fixed hexagon by `LA-EXP-DS06`'s rule: siblings are the same size, with the same text. The product is a flat-topped regular hexagon as wide as the other layouts' product box, and each cell with children MUST be split into equal-area cells for them, each within about 5% of the others, by a Voronoi diagram (a power diagram) clipped to the cell's outline inside a padding and below its header, its children a gap apart, every cell convex. The diagram is iterated until the area error is under 0.2% of the parent's area. Record counts size nothing. The layout MUST be deterministic: a parent's children start evenly round a circle about its largest inscribed point, in the tree's order clockwise from the upper left, each nudged by its ID, with a random number generator seeded by their IDs, and each parent is laid out in its own frame, so the same tree always gives the same picture, and adding one record moves nothing outside its parent's cell.

Siblings MUST share one text scale: their size (the square root of a cell's area) over 400 map units, or the largest below it at which every sibling's label fits its room, the smallest sibling cell's room deciding. A leaf's label is centered on its largest inscribed point, as wide as the cell allows there, and a parent's sits in a header at the top of its cell, its children below the header's cut, which leaves them at least 55% of the cell. A label wraps on whole words and is never clipped, so every cell shows its name (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`). A domain is a cell there, with the hexagon mark before its kind and ID line. The focus never changes the map, filters hide cells without moving the rest, and no parent lines are drawn: holding is the parent link. The layout MUST run in a web worker where there is one, and a spec loaded again with the same tree and labels MUST reuse the map it had.

title: Camera framing
statement:
Depth N MUST frame the focus, its parent at the left edge for context, and its descendants down to N levels below it, every stage, folder and group counting as a level, as in a file explorer. Depth MUST NOT add siblings or ancestors further up to the picture it frames, though the map around it stays in view. Depth stays 1 to 3, and a group at the center counts levels the same way. The side bar's lists and the summary count this framed picture. Focusing a node, by a click, the address, Back and Forward, the step keys or the trail, MUST move the camera only: it MUST frame the focus and the levels the depth shows below it to fill the pane, with the parent's level kept in view in a strip at the left edge. That opening frame MUST take whole rows of the focus's level, its edges in the gaps between them, and end on the right in the gap before the next column. A box of another branch that its top or bottom edge crosses MUST be drawn faded, at the context opacity, so the frame shows nothing cut but the parent's strip; once the person zooms or pans, every box is drawn as it is. The camera's zoom limits MUST let it frame the deepest leaf of a large product, which is very small against the product's box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), and fit the whole map in a phone's pane: 64 times the map's units at most, a ten-thousandth at least. The framed levels MUST fit the pane, however small their labels then are on screen; the depth decides only what is framed. The camera MUST move there from the view as it is, including one the person zoomed or panned, in one smooth zoom and pan (zooming out only as far as the pan needs) on the shared motion (`--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease`, at most twice the speed for a long path); on a page's first picture, on a resize and under reduced motion it MUST go there at once. Free zoom and pan move the same camera: the wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer, a drag pans, and the zoom buttons zoom about the pane's middle; a gesture during a glide takes over from it, and the frame button and the `.` command frame the focus again.

The map MUST be drawn on a canvas, anew for each frame of the camera. A viewport MUST be kept in doubles, and every map point placed on screen in doubles relative to the camera's center, with no transform but the screen's pixel ratio, so a box deep in a large map is as steady at a deep zoom as at the top. Each label's lines MUST be drawn at their size in the map times the zoom, so text is crisp at any zoom whatever the map's range. A visually hidden layer of the drawn boxes, in the keyboard's order, MUST carry focus, Tab, the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, and each box's role and name for assistive technology, and the box it focuses is drawn with the focus ring. The pointer MUST find the box under it from the map's own outlines (a box's rectangle, a shape's polygon or rounded corners, a Voronoi cell's polygon), the last drawn first, so a child drawn over its parent is found before it. In the Nested view, focusing a node by any of the ways `LA-EXP-DS09` lists MUST move the same camera, in the same glide, to frame the focus's box in the pane, within the padding and centered, within the camera's zoom limits (`LA-EXP-DS09`). The Nested camera frames the focus's box whatever the depth, so the depth control is off in the Nested view. The level of detail is `LA-EXP-DS10`'s: only boxes in view and at least 3 pixels on screen each way are drawn, each with its label, a parent before its children so a child is drawn over its parent, and a level that would take the drawing past 260 boxes is not drawn (its parents stand for it). The keyboard's order is the tree's, a parent before its children. With Links on, the focus's links MUST be drawn as curves between the drawn boxes, and edge hints point to those out of view. The Model view's camera, framing a new picture and on the Fit command, MUST fit the bounding box of all its boxes, the faded ones included, inside a margin (`LA-V94-R06`); a soft vignette of the canvas's own background MUST soften its edges.

title: Level of detail
statement: The graph MUST draw only the nodes in view (with a tenth of the pane to spare each way) and at least 3 pixels tall on screen. Every drawn node MUST show its label, its kind and ID line and its full title wrapped on whole words, at its fixed size in the map (`LA-EXP-DS06`), however small it is on screen (small text is read by zooming in): whether a node is drawn never depends on whether its text can be read, and the focus and the depth decide only what the camera frames (`LA-EXP-DS09`). Each frame the canvas MUST draw each drawn node's shape, border and fill, and its label's lines at their map size times the zoom; a line under 2 pixels on screen MAY be drawn as a faint bar where its glyphs would be, which still shows the label. A drawn node's children too small to draw MUST be one bar in their level for each run of them. Level by level from the roots, a level that would take the drawing past 260 boxes MUST be drawn as one bar per parent instead, so a product of thousands of records stays within the performance budgets (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`). The keyboard's layer of drawn boxes (`LA-EXP-DS09`) MUST take what a glide passes over once, as it starts, and be trimmed when it ends, so no frame of the glide rebuilds it.

title: ERD lines
statement: An aggregate's ERD draws exactly one line for each `has_one` and `has_many` link between its entities, one dashed line for each of its entities and each aggregate that entity's fields reference by ID, and one for each aggregate whose entities reference it; a domain's ERD draws the same for all its aggregates' entities. No line stands for anything else.

title: Record form
statement: A record's form MUST be generated from the schema description, never written per kind: one input per column of the kind's table but its ID and parent columns, typed by the column (an enum a select, a whole number a number input, true or false a check, a date a date input, a list one entry per item), its required columns marked; its parent chosen among the records of the kind's allowed parent kinds in the same product; each link's targets among the records of the kinds its relation allows, in the same product; and its part rows with their own columns. A kind a product declares MUST get its form the same way.

title: Key display
statement: Shows a binding as the platform shows it: on a Mac as the symbols ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ in Apple's order ("⇧⌘P"), elsewhere as words joined by + ("Ctrl+Shift+P"). Names each single-chord binding for `aria-keyshortcuts` with the DOM's modifier names ("Control+Shift+P"), and leaves out a sequence, which it cannot express.

title: Contrast audit
statement: Works out the WCAG contrast of each text and control token on what it is drawn on, for a theme in a mode, and which pairs fall below AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls).

title: Window placement
statement: Places a window at its saved bounds; a saved place that is no longer on a connected screen gives way to a centered window, and a size larger than the largest screen shrinks to fit it, never below the minimum size.

title: Folder to open at launch
statement: On launch, opens a folder named on the command line (unpacked or packed) or dropped on the Dock icon; else the most recent folder that still opens; else, run from Lathe's own repo, that repo; else asks for a folder.

title: Whole-ID matching
statement: Finds whether a text names an ID as a whole ID: `TL-LEND-INV05` is not found in `TL-LEND-INV050` or `TL-LEND-INV05-T`. Otherwise a test could seem to be named by a file that names another.

title: Allowed test levels
statement: Gives the run by levels each test kind allows: constraint test unit or database; invariant and specification tests unit or database; domain service test unit; policy test database, api, e2e-api, e2e-ui or manual; use case test api, e2e-api, e2e-ui or manual; view test unit, e2e-ui or manual; endpoint test contract or api; flow test e2e-ui, e2e-api or manual; integration test contract, e2e-api or manual; pattern rule test and standard rule test any.

title: Source file tracing
statement: A source file is traced when a technical record names it, or names a folder holding it. Source files are what the source globs match, less tests, configs, generated files, build output and other products' folders.

title: Route normal form
statement: Gives a route in one form, however it is written, so a record's route and the code's compare: the path alone (a query string or fragment picks a state within a page, not another page), every parameter as `{}` whatever its name or syntax (`<id>`, `:id`, `{id}`, `[id]`, a template's `${id}`, a regular expression's group or one-segment class), no repeated slash and no trailing slash but the root's. `/tools/{toolId}/damage`, `/tools/:id/damage` and `/^\/tools\/(\d+)\/damage$/` are all `/tools/{}/damage`.

title: Test case reading
statement: Reads the test cases in a test file's text, as text and never by running it: each call of `it` or `test` (with the modifiers only, skip, todo, fails, fail, fixme, slow, concurrent, sequential, skipIf, runIf and each, and Playwright's test) whose name is a string or template literal, with its line and the names of the `describe` or `test.describe` calls around it, and the IDs, as whole IDs, that those names and their `each` rows name. Strings, template literals, comments and regular expressions are skipped. A name that is not a literal, a test made by a helper function, and other runners' forms are not read.
